CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

notes: CBSA's inquire-account service (INQACC) on GENERATED Db2 rows (#4507), proving the cbsa-inqacc port on data it was not written against: 30 IBMUSER.ACCOUNT rows built from CRETB01's CREATE TABLE and CREI101's unique index (every column at its boundaries, a NULL in every nullable column, then values between; a quarter under another sort code). 40 generated LINKs: the account number each row's in turn (a fifth of the time one the table does not hold: the cursor's FETCH +100), the sort code the program's own or another (the cursor ignores INQACC-SCODE). A generated NULL last-statement date reaches FETCH -305 (no indicator) and the ABNDPROC LINK and ABNDFILE record; the 99999999 sentinel is pinned as a hand scenario (READ-ACCOUNT-LAST). Every task's statements are compared with what Db2 answered (compare_sql), and ACCOUNT and ABNDFILE after every task. Burned estate (CBSA).

scenarios.name: last-account-sentinel
scenarios.why: INQACC-ACCNO 99999999: READ-ACCOUNT-LAST's SELECT ... ORDER BY ACCOUNT_NUMBER DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROW gives the highest account of sort code 987654 (99999998), 'Y'
